utterances.text: Well, if you want to testify, maybe you should call yourself as a witness. I can tell you that there were camps. They are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is an inappropriate comment, Dr. Donia. We'll control the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just compose yourself. We're coming to the end now. We have two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can he answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just answer the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is quite enough. And you know that people were being killed in camps, slaughtered and thrown into containers?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the last question, because you quoted this personally somewhere, I'm not defending Mladic here, nor do I care to, but this man here was under the command of General Mladic. Did Mladic ever state this: People and nations are not -- are not dummies. We cannot wage war on every front line nor against every people. We would like us to be as smart as to not to go into every war, and if we are attacked we will defend ourselves. We don't want the war against the Muslim people nor against the Croatian people but against those who started the war and drove these people -- made those people attack us. Do you know of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is my friend quoting from a document, attributing it to Mladic, and if he is, perhaps we could know the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have another question, too, but let us clear that up first. You asked did Mladic ever state this, and then you went on to -- is that a quotation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it in my notes from the time when I was amicus curiae. And there was a number of documents drafted by Mr. Donia, and I have those in my notes, and these are Mr. Donia's quote from -- of a Mladic's statement at an assembly. If he remembers, all right, if not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of that, Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President, and I did cite it earlier. I would like to also apologise to you, sir, for my inappropriate remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tapuskovic, in that question, you said this man here, meaning the accused was under the command of General Mladic. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was trying to say that probably then he respected the position of a man who was his superior, meaning that it wasn't his wish to wage war against any people but probably the words uttered by his commander also reflect his feelings. I would like to finish my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Has he ever read an order anywhere to shoot at civilians and citizens of Sarajevo? Have you ever found such an order?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it, and you may now leave. We will adjourn until Tuesday, the -- Monday, the 26th, at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.03 p.m.,
